description: The RFC 8446 §4.1.1 TLS 1.3 full-handshake message sequence as orderable cards for the build-and-break round. The tls13-sim runs the §A.1 state machine: the canonical order reaches the established state; ApplicationData before both Finished raises the real unexpected_message(10); a legacy-only ClientHello raises protocol_version(70); an expired Certificate raises certificate_expired(45).

provenance.reference: RFC 8446 §4.1.1 (message flow: ClientHello, ServerHello, {EncryptedExtensions, Certificate, CertificateVerify, Finished}, {Finished}), §A.1 (client/server state machine), §6.2 + the IANA TLS Alert Registry (the numeric AlertDescription codes)
provenance.reproducible_against: a real `openssl s_client -connect host:443 -tls1_3` exchange produces this message order; the negotiated 'New, TLSv1.3, Cipher is …' line confirms the full handshake
provenance.verified_codes: unexpected_message=10, handshake_failure=40, bad_certificate=42, certificate_expired=45, protocol_version=70 — the literal RFC 8446 §6.2 / IANA registry values
provenance.honesty_note: Authored from RFC 8446 with citation (the message NAMES and the alert CODES are the spec's literal values); the state machine is the consequence engine — the alert a wrong move raises is computed, not authored.
